clue.text: Contrivance for bouncers and top railmen, perhaps

indicators.note: perhaps hints that the words top railmen may be a version of something else, so their letters are to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A gadget for nightclub doormen and senior railway workers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bouncers' suggests nightclub doormen, but here they are people bouncing on a springy mat; 'perhaps' tells you to rearrange TOP RAILMEN.
explanation.definitionFit: A springy canvas sheet stretched on a frame is equipment designed for people who jump up and down on it.

clue.text: Pastry confection containing no game

indicators.note: containing means the pastry word holds the other piece inside it

parts.note: a tart is a pastry dish with a filling
no as a quantity is nought, written as the letter O

explanation.surface: A pastry dish made without any venison or pheasant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'game' looks like meat for the pie, but it is the definition: a card game.
explanation.definitionFit: Tarot is a card game played across Europe with a pack of seventy-eight cards, also used for fortune-telling.

clue.text: Food article — it's on tap when cooked

parts.note: a is the indefinite article in grammar

indicators.note: cooking changes the ingredients, so the letters of it's on tap are mixed up

explanation.surface: A food item that is always available from the tap once prepared.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when cooked' rearranges the letters of 'it's on tap' (NTIPASTO), placed after the article; the surface pictures a dish served on tap.
explanation.definitionFit: Antipasto is the Italian starter course of cold meats, olives and pickles, served as food before the main dish.

clue.text: Tingling sensation familiar to seamstresses

explanation.surface: A prickly feeling in the limbs, well known to people who sew.
explanation.definitionFit: The prickly feeling in a limb as numbness wears off has this name; literally, sewing tools are what every dressmaker handles daily.

clue.text: Propensity for gaining knowledge right away

indicators.note: away tells you the letter for right is sent off from the longer word

parts.note: learning is the act of gaining knowledge

explanation.surface: A natural tendency for picking up knowledge quickly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'right away' reads as 'immediately', but it splits: R (right) is taken away from LEARNING.
explanation.definitionFit: A leaning is an inclination or tendency towards something.

clue.text: Solvent dissolving more than half of 23? Gosh!

indicators.note: dissolving breaks the letters up so they re-form in a new order, apt for a chemical surface

parts.note: 23 across is SYCOPHANT, nine letters; its last five, more than half, are PHANT
ah is an exclamation of surprise, like gosh

explanation.surface: A solvent breaking down most of a crossword answer, with a cry of surprise.
explanation.walkthrough: The cross-reference is to 23 across; 'dissolving' rearranges PHANT plus AH.
explanation.definitionFit: Naphtha is a volatile petroleum liquid used to dissolve oils and rubber, a classic industrial solvent.

clue.text: Island state taken with Hitler's agreement?

parts.note: ja is German for yes, so it is what a German leader would say to agree
VA is the postal abbreviation for the US state of Virginia

explanation.surface: An island nation annexed with the Führer's consent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hitler's agreement' simply means a German yes.
explanation.definitionFit: Java is the main island of Indonesia, home to its capital Jakarta.

clue.text: Surrounded by silver, a Scotsman divides it

indicators.note: divides means this piece splits the silver symbol in two by sitting between its letters

parts.note: Ag is the chemical symbol for silver
mon is a Scots spelling of man

explanation.surface: A Scot splitting up a hoard of silver.
explanation.walkthrough: The page prints 'Scotsman' as one word; the OCR text broke it up.
explanation.definitionFit: Among means in the midst of, encircled by others.

clue.text: A levy is raised, intended, it's said, for distribution

indicators.note: in a down clue, raised means the word is written from bottom to top, so backwards

parts.note: a toll is a charge or levy

indicators.note: it's said marks a word that is only spoken, to be written another way with the same sound

parts.note: meant is a synonym for intended

explanation.surface: A tax is put up, supposedly to be shared out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is raised' turns TOLL to LLOT in this down entry; MEANT spoken gives the ending MENT.
explanation.definitionFit: An allotment is a share handed out, or the act of dividing something up and allocating it.

clue.text: Attendant demon not unaccustomed to strong drink

parts.note: familiar with something means not unaccustomed to it
spirit is distilled alcohol such as whisky or gin

explanation.surface: A demon in service who is no stranger to the bottle.
explanation.walkthrough: A familiar spirit is the demon companion said to serve a witch.
explanation.definitionFit: In folklore a witch's companion, often a cat or toad, was a devil assigned to wait upon her.

clue.text: Composed a letter beneath, say, the Round House

indicators.note: say marks that the words are to be spoken, giving a word spelt differently

parts.note: writing a letter underneath something is to have wrote under it, which spoken runs together

explanation.surface: A note written underneath, directed to a famous circular building.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wrote under', spoken quickly, gives the sound of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A rotunda is a building or hall that is circular in plan, usually domed.

clue.text: Thomas Love or his wife?

parts.note: Thomas Love Peacock was an English novelist; the male bird he is named for, or its mate the peahen, belongs to one species

explanation.surface: A question about a man named Thomas Love, or perhaps his spouse.
explanation.walkthrough: You need the novelist's surname: complete it and his 'wife' becomes the female bird.
explanation.definitionFit: Peacocks and peahens together make up the species, a large ornamental pheasant.

clue.text: Leading journalist gives away daughter to woodcutter

parts.note: top means leading or foremost

indicators.note: gives away means the journalist loses a letter, punning on a father giving away a bride

parts.note: a diarist keeps a journal, so is literally a journal-ist

explanation.surface: A top reporter hands his daughter in marriage to a lumberjack.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gives away daughter' suggests a wedding but means D is dropped; a 'journalist' here is one who writes a journal.
explanation.definitionFit: A topiarist clips hedges and shrubs into shapes, so is one who cuts living wood.

clue.text: Being trendy, obtained gold bar

parts.note: in means fashionable or trendy
got is the past tense of get, meaning obtained

explanation.surface: Being fashionable, someone acquired a bar of gold.
explanation.definitionFit: An ingot is a block of cast metal, typically precious metal such as gold.

clue.text: Grounded when retired

annotationWithheld.why: Grounded when retired (5): the only parse is AS (when) inside BED, with 'retired' giving both BED and the containment, one word doing two jobs

clue.text: Ban quartz in the interior of a hall

indicators.note: in the interior means one piece goes inside the other's middle

parts.note: quartz is the crystalline form of silica, silicon dioxide

explanation.surface: Quartz is prohibited inside a large hall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in the interior of a hall' reads as one phrase, but 'of a hall' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A basilica is a large oblong hall, Roman or church; the adjective means relating to such a building.

clue.text: Be attracted to French comic actor's return in serious setting

indicators.note: in means the returned name sits inside the other piece

parts.note: grave means serious, and here it forms the setting round the other letters

indicators.note: return means the actor's name is written backwards

parts.note: Jacques Tati was the French comic actor and director of Monsieur Hulot's Holiday

explanation.surface: Feeling drawn to a French comedian's comeback in a solemn role.
explanation.walkthrough: 'return' reverses the actor's surname to ITAT; the stray mark after 'to' in the text is a smudge on the page.
explanation.definitionFit: To gravitate is to move towards or be drawn to something, as if pulled by gravity.

clue.text: Downfall of man holding up woman -husband enters

indicators.note: in a down clue, the man holding up the woman means he is written below her

parts.note: Ava is a woman's name

indicators.note: enters means the husband letter goes inside the man's name

parts.note: Lance is a man's name

explanation.surface: A man lifting a woman while her husband walks in.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry, 'holding up' means the man is written below the woman; 'enters' slips the husband letter into him.
explanation.definitionFit: An avalanche is a sudden fall of a mass of snow down a mountainside.

clue.text: Device which initially scared brown donkey trapped by unruly mob

indicators.note: trapped by means the donkey is shut inside those two opening letters
initially takes the opening letter of each of the two words that follow

parts.note: moke is British slang for a donkey

indicators.note: unruly means the letters of mob are out of order

explanation.surface: A frightened brown donkey cornered by a disorderly crowd.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially' gives S and B, which trap MOKE; 'unruly' turns MOB into OMB.
explanation.definitionFit: A smoke bomb is a device that releases a cloud when set off, used for cover or signalling.

clue.text: Outside an American state, to live in one is indecent

indicators.note: in means the combined piece goes inside the word for one

parts.note: one is written out in full

indicators.note: outside means the verb for living goes round the state

parts.note: to be is to exist or live
SC is the abbreviation for South Carolina

explanation.surface: Living alone beyond the borders of a US state is shameful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Outside' wraps the verb round the state; 'in' then sets that block, BSCE, inside the written-out number.
explanation.definitionFit: Obscene means offensive to accepted standards of decency, especially in sexual matters.

clue.text: Champion book! Outstanding work!

parts.note: to champion a cause is to back it
a log is a book of records, as a ship's log

explanation.surface: Two cheers: a winning book and a brilliant piece of work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Outstanding' reads as 'excellent' but means 'still to be done'.
explanation.definitionFit: A backlog is an accumulation of tasks still waiting to be dealt with.

clue.text: Right drying room heat

parts.note: an oast is a kiln or building for drying hops

explanation.surface: The right room for drying things, given the heat.
explanation.walkthrough: An oast house is the kiln with a cowled roof used in southern England to dry hops.
explanation.definitionFit: To roast is to cook with dry heat in an oven or over a fire, so it means to heat strongly.

clue.text: Ghastly hat incorporating a lot of fur

indicators.note: incorporating means the hat word takes the other piece into its body

parts.note: lid is slang for a hat

indicators.note: a lot of means most but not all of the word fur, so its first letter is dropped

explanation.surface: A hideous hat trimmed with plenty of fur.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a lot of' trims fur to UR; 'incorporating' puts that inside the hat. 'Ghastly' here means pale and gruesome.
explanation.definitionFit: Lurid means shocking or gruesome, as in horribly vivid detail.

clue.text: Capital outlay at first for an ardent lover

parts.note: Rome is the capital of Italy

indicators.note: at first means only the opening letter of outlay is taken

explanation.surface: Spending on a capital city, from the start, for a passionate suitor.
explanation.walkthrough: Shakespeare's young lover gives his name to any passionate suitor.
explanation.definitionFit: A Romeo is a man devoted to wooing women, after Shakespeare's hero.

clue.text: Stony chap — awful bootlicker

indicators.note: awful means terribly made, so the letters of stony chap are rearranged

explanation.surface: A hard-faced man who is a dreadful toady.
explanation.definitionFit: A sycophant flatters powerful people to win favour, a fawning toady.

clue.text: Stories of hastily summoned jurors

explanation.surface: Accounts of jurors who were called up in a rush.
explanation.definitionFit: Stories are narratives; in English law the word also names jurors drafted from bystanders to make up a short panel.

clue.text: MC's agent returned income

indicators.note: the word income is split, so in tells you the returned agent goes inside come
returned means the agent word is written backwards

parts.note: a rep is a representative or agent

explanation.surface: A master of ceremonies' manager sent back his earnings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'income' must be split as 'in come'; 'returned' turns the agent round to PER. COMPÈRE is the British word for a show's host.
explanation.definitionFit: A compère is the host who introduces acts at a show, the British term for a master of ceremonies.

clue.text: We may wax this, given sufficient enthusiasm

definitions.text: We may wax this, given sufficient enthusiasm

parts.words: We may wax this, given sufficient enthusiasm
parts.note: the idiom 'to wax' plus an adjective means to speak in an increasingly effusive way about something, as people do when enthused

explanation.surface: A remark about polishing something if we are keen enough.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wax' looks like polishing, but it means grow or become, as in the idiom for gushing.
explanation.definitionFit: To wax in this way is to talk with great, song-like enthusiasm about a subject.

clue.text: Small number acting at this time

parts.note: no is the short form of number
on means performing on stage, acting

explanation.surface: A small cast performing at a particular hour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Small number' means an abbreviated 'number', NO.
explanation.definitionFit: Noon is midday, twelve o'clock, a fixed hour of the day.

clue.text: Be subject to fewer delays, say, as astronauts may be

indicators.note: say signals that the words are to be spoken and give a word spelt another way

parts.note: to be kept waiting less is to wait less, which spoken matches another word

explanation.surface: Hoping for shorter queues, as space travellers might.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wait less', spoken, gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: In orbit astronauts are in free fall and feel no gravity, floating as if without mass.
